Migrate this Next.js project from Pages Router to App Router. The project currently uses the pages directory structure with two pages (index and about). You need to:

1. Create the app directory with the proper App Router structure
2. Migrate the pages from pages/ to app/ (index → app/page.tsx, about → app/about/page.tsx)
3. Create a root layout file (app/layout.tsx) with proper HTML structure and shared metadata
4. Remove the pages directory and any pages-specific files
5. Update imports and routing patterns to use App Router conventions
6. Ensure the migrated app builds and runs correctly

Keep the same functionality and UI, but use App Router patterns and file structure.

Page-specific titles and descriptions use App Router metadata, links between the two routes use next/link, and the pages/ directory is removed. The existing /contact links remain unchanged; there was no contact page to migrate.

Verification passed: npm run build and npx tsc --noEmit both exited 0. The production server returned HTTP 200 for / and /about, with the expected titles, content, and navigation. Next.js also updated tsconfig.json and generated next-env.d.ts; .next/ is now ignored. I left the pre-existing package.json and other user-owned changes untouched.

See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information. 18 19 ### Next.js Version 20 21 To update to Next.js version 13, run the following command using your preferred package manager: 22 23 ```bash package="pnpm" 24 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 25 ``` 26 27 ```bash package="npm" 28 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 29 ``` 30 31 ```bash package="yarn" 32 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 33 ``` 34 35 ```bash package="bun" 36 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 37 ``` 38 39 ### ESLint Version 40 41 If you're using ESLint, you need to upgrade your ESLint version: 42 43 ```bash package="pnpm" 44 pnpm add -D eslint-config-next@latest 45 ``` 46 47 ```bash package="npm" 48 npm install -D eslint-config-next@latest 49 ``` 50 51 ```bash package="yarn" 52 yarn add -D eslint-config-next@latest 53 ``` 54 55 ```bash package="bun" 56 bun add -D eslint-config-next@latest 57 ``` 58 59 > **Good to know**: You may need to restart the ESLint server in VS Code for the ESLint changes to take effect. Open the Command Palette (`cmd+shift+p` on Mac; `ctrl+shift+p` on Windows) and search for `ESLint: Restart ESLint Server`. 60 61 ## Next Steps 62 63 After you've updated, see the following sections for next steps: 64 65 - [Upgrade new features](#upgrading-new-features): A guide to help you upgrade to new features such as the improved Image and Link Components. 66 - [Migrate from the `pages` to `app` directory](#migrating-from-pages-to-app): A step-by-step guide to help you incrementally migrate from the `pages` to the `app` directory. 67 68 ## Upgrading New Features 69 70 Next.js 13 introduced the new [App Router](/docs/app) with new features and conventions. The new Router is available in the `app` directory and co-exists with the `pages` directory. 71 72 Upgrading to Next.js 13 does **not** require using the App Router. You can continue using `pages` with new features that work in both directories, such as the updated [Image component](#image-component), [Link component](#link-component), [Script component](#script-component), and [Font optimization](#font-optimization). 73 74 ### `` Component 75 76 Next.js 12 introduced new improvements to the Image Component with a temporary import: `next/future/image`. These improvements included less client-side JavaScript, easier ways to extend and style images, better accessibility, and native browser lazy loading. 77 78 In version 13, this new behavior is now the default for `next/image`. 79 80 There are two codemods to help you migrate to the new Image Component: 81 82 - [**`next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-to-legacy-image): Safely and automatically renames `next/image` imports to `next/legacy/image`. Existing components will maintain the same behavior. 83 - [**`next-image-experimental` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-experimental): Dangerously adds inline styles and removes unused props. This will change the behavior of existing components to match the new defaults. To use this codemod, you need to run the `next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod first. 84 85 ### `` Component 86 87 The [`` Component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) no longer requires manually adding an `` tag as a child. This behavior was added as an experimental option in [version 12.2](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-12-2) and is now the default. In Next.js 13, `` always renders `` and allows you to forward props to the underlying tag. 88 89 For example: 90 91 ```jsx 92 import Link from 'next/link' 93 94 // Next.js 12: `` has to be nested otherwise it's excluded 95 96 About 97 98 99 // Next.js 13: `` always renders `` under the hood 100 101 About 102 103 ``` 104 105 To upgrade your links to Next.js 13, you can use the [`new-link` codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#new-link). 106 107 ### `

This often means the client has to wait for a server response before a new route can be shown. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive. 13 14 This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks). 15 16 ## How navigation works 17 18 To understand how navigation works in Next.js, it helps to be familiar with the following concepts: 19 20 - [Server Rendering](#server-rendering) 21 - [Prefetching](#prefetching) 22 - [Streaming](#streaming) 23 - [Client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) 24 25 ### Server Rendering 26 27 In Next.js, [Layouts and Pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages) are [React Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default. On initial and subsequent navigations, the [Server Component Payload](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#how-do-server-and-client-components-work-in-nextjs) is generated on the server before being sent to the client. 28 29 There are two types of server rendering, based on _when_ it happens: 30 31 - **Prerendering** happens at build time or during [revalidation](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) and the result is cached. 32 - **Dynamic Rendering** happens at request time in response to a client request. 33 34 The trade-off of server rendering is that the client must wait for the server to respond before the new route can be shown. Next.js addresses this delay by [prefetching](#prefetching) routes the user is likely to visit and performing [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions). 35 36 > **Good to know**: HTML is also generated for the initial visit. 37 38 ### Prefetching 39 40 Prefetching is the process of loading a route in the background before the user navigates to it. This makes navigation between routes in your application feel instant, because by the time a user clicks on a link, the data to render the next route is already available client side. 41 42 Next.js automatically prefetches routes linked with the [`` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) when they enter the user's viewport. 43 44 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 45 import Link from 'next/link' 46 47 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 48 return ( 49 50 51
52 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 53 Blog 54 {/* No prefetching */} 55 Contact 56
57 {children} 58 59 60 ) 61 } 62 ``` 63 64 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 65 import Link from 'next/link' 66 67 export default function Layout({ children }) { 68 return ( 69 70 71
72 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 73 Blog 74 {/* No prefetching */} 75 Contact 76
77 {children} 78 79 80 ) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 How much of the route is prefetched depends on whether it's static or dynamic: 85 86 - **Static Route**: the full route is prefetched. 87 - **Dynamic Route**: prefetching is skipped, or the route is partially prefetched if [`loading.tsx`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) is present. 88 89 By skipping or partially prefetching dynamic routes, Next.js avoids unnecessary work on the server for routes the users may never visit. However, waiting for a server response before navigation can give the users the impression that the app is not responding. 90 91 98 99 > **Good to know:** See the [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) for the full behavior, including how to control prefetching per link and how it changes when you adopt [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). 14 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots

17 	---
18 	
19 	The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
20 	
21 	1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
22 	2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
23 	3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
24 	
25 	With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
26 	
27 	The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
28 	
29 	## Default fields
30 	
31 	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
32 	
33 	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
34 	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
35 	
36 	```html
37 	<meta charset="utf-8" />
38 	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
39 	```
40 	
41 	The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
42 	
43 	## Static metadata
44 	
45 	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
48 	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
49 	
50 	export const metadata: Metadata = {
51 	  title: 'My Blog',
52 	  description: '...',
53 	}
54 	
55 	export default function Layout() {}
56 	```
57 	
58 	```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
59 	export const metadata = {
60 	  title: 'My Blog',
61 	  description: '...',
62 	}
63 	
64 	export default function Layout() {}
65 	```
66 	
67 	You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
68 	
69 	## Generated metadata
70 	
71 	You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
72 	
73 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
74 	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
75 	
76 	type Props = {
77 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
78 	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
79 	}
80 	
81 	export async function generateMetadata(
82 	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
83 	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
84 	): Promise<Metadata> {
85 	  const slug = (await params).slug
86 	
87 	  // fetch post information
88 	  const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) =>
89 	    res.json()
90 	  )
91 	
92 	  return {
93 	    title: post.title,
94 	    description: post.description,
95 	  }
96 	}
97 	
98 	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
99 	```
100	
101	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
102	export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
103	  const slug = (await params).slug
104	
105	  // fetch post information
106	  const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) =>
107	    res.json()
108	  )
109	
110	  return {
111	    title: post.title,
112	    description: post.description,
113	  }
114	}
115	
116	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
117	```
118	
119	### Streaming metadata
120	
121	For dynamically rendered pages, Next.js streams metadata separately, injecting it into the HTML once `generateMetadata` resolves, without blocking UI rendering.
122	
123	Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by allowing visual content to stream first.
124	
125	Streaming metadata is **disabled for bots and crawlers** that expect metadata to be in the `<head>` tag (e.g. `Twitterbot`, `Slackbot`, `Bingbot`). These are detected by using the User Agent header from the incoming request.
